sources.title: Linux user namespaces and namespace-scoped capabilities
sources.version_or_date: Linux man-pages 6.19; manual dated 2026-02-08; HTML rendering 2026-09-09
sources.sections_read: Description; Capabilities; Effect of capabilities; interaction with other namespaces; beginning of UID/GID mappings. Colophon and dated footer.
sources.confirmed: User namespaces can present UID 0 internally while mapping to an unprivileged outside UID; capabilities apply to resources governed by the owning user namespace. UID and GID maps are defined through per-process proc files.
sources.limits: Create associated resource namespaces under the correct user namespace; kernel vulnerabilities remain possible. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: post_decision. Original read and any failures remain in runs/A/C02.json.

sources.title: Docker Engine userns-remap
sources.sections_read: Introduction; About remapping and subordinate user and group IDs; Prerequisites; beginning of Enable userns-remap. Disable namespace remapping; User namespace known limitations.
sources.confirmed: Docker remaps workload UID/GID ranges while its daemon remains root, with bind-mount ownership requirements. Its documentation lists incompatibilities with host PID/network sharing and fully privileged mode unless remapping is disabled.
sources.limits: Daemon-level configuration does not supply pod allocation policy; bind mounts and fully privileged or host-namespace modes require care. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: unknown. Original read and any failures remain in runs/A/C02.json.

sources.title: LXD isolated per-container identity maps
sources.sections_read: Introduction; Increasing the size of the default map; Per container maps.
sources.confirmed: The dated LXD post describes distinct nonoverlapping UID/GID ranges per container through security.idmap.isolated, configurable range size, and the ownership/sharing cost of remapping its filesystem.
sources.limits: Requires sufficient subordinate IDs; filesystem remapping costs time and distinct maps complicate shared storage. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: pre_decision. Original read and any failures remain in runs/A/C02.json.

sources.title: Podman v4.3 automatic user-namespace allocation
sources.version_or_date: Podman v4.3 manual; v4.3.0 release dated 2022-10-22 in opened official archive
sources.sections_read: Name, synopsis, description, image transports; --user and --userns=mode including auto options.
sources.confirmed: Podman v4.3 documents auto allocation of unique UID/GID ranges from subordinate-ID pools, image-based or explicit range sizing, and joining another container's user namespace.
sources.limits: Needs subordinate-ID pools; adapt allocation and lifetime from container scope to pod scope. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: pre_decision. Original read and any failures remain in runs/A/C02.json.

sources.title: Linux idmapped mounts
sources.sections_read: Introduction; Formal notes; Idmappings on idmapped mounts and filesystem versus mount ownership.
sources.confirmed: The kernel document explains how idmapped mounts translate ownership per mount, enabling differently mapped containers to access a filesystem without a global recursive ownership rewrite.
sources.limits: Requires supporting kernel/filesystem combinations and deliberate sharing policy; it does not itself allocate pod IDs. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: unknown. Original read and any failures remain in runs/A/C02.json.

sources.title: Firecracker specialized virtual-machine monitor
sources.confirmed: The NSDI 2020 paper describes a specialized virtual-machine monitor for isolating container and function workloads. This supplies an alternative virtualization mechanism rather than a UID/GID allocator.
sources.limits: Requires a larger runtime architecture change and does not supply the requested host UID/GID allocation policy. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: pre_decision. Original read and any failures remain in runs/A/C02.json.

sources.title: config.go
sources.sections_read: IDMap; UIDMappings; GIDMappings; related security configuration fields.
sources.confirmed: The actual public runc configuration source defines separate UID and GID mapping lists with container start ID, host start ID, and range size. This source was opened via web-indexed code after direct raw retrieval failed.
sources.limits: This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: unknown. Original read and any failures remain in runs/A/C02.json.

sources.title: runc libcontainer mapping structures and example
sources.sections_read: UIDMappings and GIDMappings example; container creation and UID 0 process example.
sources.confirmed: The libcontainer example maps container IDs beginning at zero to host IDs beginning at 1000 for both UID and GID, then shows creating the container and launching an internal UID 0 process. Its literal host range is example data, not a safe allocation policy for all hosts.
sources.limits: Reserve safe host ranges instead of copying the sample host ID; current branch evidence is undated. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: unknown. Original read and any failures remain in runs/A/C02.json.

sources.title: OCI runtime-spec user-namespace configuration
sources.version_or_date: Live main branch; older tagged version could not be fetched
sources.sections_read: Namespaces creation/join behavior; User namespace mappings; example; related devices section.
sources.confirmed: The OCI source specifies separate UID/GID mapping arrays with containerID, hostID and size, and namespace creation or joining through type and path. It says filesystem ownership should not be modified merely to realize these mappings.
sources.limits: The orchestrator must allocate ranges and handle filesystems; the older tagged document could not be retrieved. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: unknown. Original read and any failures remain in runs/A/C02.json.
